name: Employability & Workplace Skills

objectives.text: Identify workplace habits that make someone a reliable worker, such as punctuality, following directions, and finishing tasks
Demonstrate responsibility by completing an assigned agricultural chore, such as feeding animals or watering a garden, on schedule and without reminders
Describe the skills needed to work safely and effectively in an agricultural workplace
Explain why honesty and integrity matter to employers, coworkers, and customers in an agricultural business
Demonstrate respectful workplace communication with adults, including a proper greeting, eye contact, a firm handshake, and clear speech
Use a planner or calendar to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines for school and agricultural responsibilities
Explain the steps of applying for a job, including a résumé, application, and interview
Identify the career and personal management skills, such as time management, planning, and prioritizing, that employers in AFNR workplaces expect
Apply time management, goal setting, and prioritizing skills to manage the daily responsibilities of a supervised agricultural experience
Complete a job application for an agricultural position accurately, neatly, and with appropriate references
Apply professional communication and teamwork skills to engage team members in completing a group agricultural project
Demonstrate professional workplace conduct, including appropriate dress, phone and email etiquette, and following company policies
Analyze a workplace problem in an agricultural setting using critical thinking and propose a workable solution
Explain how human resources functions such as hiring, performance evaluation, compensation, and record keeping affect employees in AFNR businesses
Evaluate one's own leadership and workplace strengths and areas for growth through a self-assessment in preparation for an agricultural career
Analyze the strategies AFNR employers use to recruit, train, and retain employees and judge their effectiveness
Evaluate workplace behaviors that build positive morale and culture, such as recognizing others' skills and promoting collaboration
Develop a personal improvement plan in response to supervisor feedback from a placement SAE or employer evaluation
Demonstrate effective interview skills in a mock interview modeled on the FFA Employment Skills Leadership Development Event
Evaluate appropriate responses to ethical dilemmas in an agricultural workplace, such as a safety violation or an animal welfare concern
Develop a résumé, cover letter, and interview strategy for a specific agricultural job or internship
Create a professional portfolio that documents SAE records, FFA achievements, certifications, and work samples for employers

changes: Kept all six existing objectives with light rewording: reliable habits (4), safe and effective work skills (6), job application steps (8), teamwork on a group project (10), self-assessment (11), and résumé, cover letter, and interview strategy (12). Added middle grade competencies on carrying out chores responsibly, integrity, respectful communication, and time management. Added high school competencies tied to the listed standards: personal management in SAE, completing a job application, professional conduct, workplace problem solving, human resources from the employee's view, employer recruitment and retention strategies, building workplace morale, responding to supervisor feedback, mock interviews modeled on the FFA Employment Skills LDE, workplace ethics, and a professional portfolio. Career exploration, enterprise planning, and cooperatives are left to the sibling sub-topics.
